newsitem.title: UK: GEC discusses change to Simpson's package.
newsitem.headline: GEC discusses change to Simpson's package.

text.p: British defence and engineering group General Electric Co, under attack over the generous pay proposals for its new managing director George Simpson, has discussed making changes to the package, industry sources said.
The company on Monday proposed draft changes to Simpson's remuneration. GEC representatives earlier met the Association of British Insurers' head of investment affairs Richard Regan.

The meeting had been called after shareholders expressed concern over the terms of Simpson's proposed 10 million stg pay package. They were angered that performance criteria Simpson had to meet to receive a huge block of shares were not tough enough.
"Some changes have been made in response to the indications of the ABI," said a source who declined to be named. "It is a draft amendement, which the company has discussed with the ABI."

The source declined to specify what the proposed changes were. Without amendment, Simpson would receive the share options if GEC's share price beat the FTSE 100 index by 10 percent in any six months within a specified three year period.
His three year contract includes annual pay of up to 1.5 million stg, including pension contributions and share options.
Nobody at GEC was immediately able to comment. Investors Norwich Union and Prudential Corp declined to comment.
